As we age, it is common to see signs of ageing on our skin. From wrinkles, fine lines, age spots, sagging skin and dryer and rougher skin, these “imperfections” have spurred many people to seek flawless skin. At the same time, they are physical evidence that our skin has been working hard amidst all the harsh environmental and emotional factors.

To renew your skin’s radiance and stay youthful-looking, you can always introduce skin rejuvenation facial treatments. These facial treatments focus on revitalizing your complexion and reducing signs of ageing. In this article, you will also learn more about the benefits of skin rejuvenation treatments, and the different types of treatments available, and explore the art of maintaining your skin’s health.

It’s time to embrace a new chapter of self-confidence and reveal new skin to help you achieve that glowing and youthful look.

blocks.text: What is skin rejuvenation facial treatment?
blocks.html: What is skin rejuvenation facial treatment?

Skin rejuvenation treatments usually involve removing old skin layers and stimulating collagen regrowth in the skin by enhancing the production of . This process is especially important to combat anti-ageing since it helps to tighten connective tissues in the skin and remove blemishes on the surface. For skin to appear youthul, collagen production has to be optimized.

Skin rejuvenation also treats other skin issues such as:

  • Wrinkles
  • Pigmentation from sun damage
  • Pigmentation
  • Stubborn scars
  • Skin redness
  • Enlarged pores
  • Uneven skin texture
How Does It Work?

Skin rejuvenation facials are non-invasive and do not have the complications of invasive medical procedures. These facials aim to improve skin texture and tighten facial complexion. Usually, professional exfoliation is done as part of the facial to remove old dull skin cells, to make way for younger skin cells. This exfoliation process also stimulates collagen production and the skin’s self-healing properties – key components for skin renewal.
Types of skin rejuvenation treatments
There are various ways to achieve skin rejuvenation. Depending on your skin type, goals and preference, there would always one that suits you. Here are some popular skin rejuvenation facials.
Microermabrasion (also known as diamond peel)

Microdermabrasion is a non-invasive cosmetic procedure commonly used in skin rejuvenation treatment to improve the overall texture and appearance of the skin. It involves the mechanical exfoliation of the outermost layer of the skin, known as the stratum corneum, using a diamond-tipped wand. This process helps to remove dead skin cells, promote cell turnover, and stimulate collagen production

Microdermabrasion is often used to address various skin concerns, including dullness, fine lines, mild acne scars, uneven skin texture, and hyperpigmentation. It is generally considered a safe and well-tolerated procedure, suitable for individuals with different skin types. However, the number of sessions needed and the intensity of the treatment may vary depending on individual skin conditions and desired outcomes.
Microneedling

A microneedling device, which can be a dermaroller or an automated pen-like device, is gently rolled or moved across the skin. The device contains tiny, sterile needles that create controlled micro-injuries in the skin. This process stimulates the body’s natural wound healing response, leading to the production of collagen and elastin, which are essential for maintaining skin elasticity and firmness. With this treatment, the results are undeniably fast as they directly target the skin’s epidermis to bring about rejuvenation

It’s important to note that microneedling should be performed by a trained and qualified skincare professional or dermatologist to ensure safety and optimal results. The number of sessions required depends on individual skin conditions and treatment goals. Microneedling is generally considered a safe and well-tolerated procedure, and the downtime is typically minimal compared to more invasive treatments.
Chemical Peels (mild/superficial)

Chemical peel facials are used to address a variety of skin concerns, including fine lines, wrinkles, uneven skin tone, acne scars, and sun damage. Superficial peels target the outermost layer of the skin (epidermis) and are generally well-tolerated with minimal downtime.
Manual Facials

This category of facials appeals to those that want a natural approach. Such facials involve the use of massage techniques to lift facial contours and stimulate collagen production. Some would use TCM (Traditional Chinese Medicine) methods to improve circulation in the face, which helps create radiance and skin rejuvenation.
Technology Facials

Skin rejuvenation technology facials encompass a variety of advanced treatments designed to enhance the appearance and health of the skin. Here are some of the commonly used ones like laser skin rejuvenation as they have proven to be beneficial: IPL skin rejuvenation (Intense Pulsed Light), RF (Radiofrequency) and Ultrasound.

Different technologies use different modes to achieve collagen stimulation and to improve skin texture.

items.q: How long does it take for results to show?
items.a: It is common to see visible results from the first session, but we would recommend attending several sessions, around 3 to 6 treatments, to see your desired results.

items.q: Are follow-up sessions necessary or needed?
items.a: To get the most out of your skin rejuvenation treatments and keep the results consistent, you can choose to do a follow-up session based on your desired results. For deeper scars, you can also do extra sessions to permanently treat these skin issues.

items.q: How to maintain the results of the treatment?
items.a:
After every skin rejuvenation treatment, it is always good to incorporate quality skincare into your regimen. Not only does this ensure that the results from the treatment stay longer, but your skin is consistently well taken care of. To maintain or extend the results of your skin rejuvenation treatment, here are some extra tips for you:

  • Avoid sun exposure and always wear sunblock, at least SPF30 and above
  • Hydrate your skin regularly with serums, moisturisers or facial masks
  • Follow a personalised skincare routine catered to your skin
  • Follow up with treatments every 1-2 months
